parsed.explanation: Documented traveller-facing exposures are substantial. Facility bans cover government buildings in roughly 19 states plus one more, and 6 extend to some private settings. Four states make certain bathroom use criminal, and one documented arrest led to 24 hours held in a men's ward, which is birth-sex custody. Entry screening can refuse applicants over document discrepancies, and trans travellers have had passports confiscated or blocked, leaving some stranded. Federal rhetoric frames pro-trans groups as a counterterrorism priority. Offsetting factors: no national sodomy law, national hate-crime and employment protections, anti-discrimination law in 22 states plus DC, and courts blocking several measures. Violence is undocumented, and the corrections and custody-abuse claims are uncorroborated, so they are excluded. The 'do not travel' tally is unsourced. Overall this sits in the elevated-to-high band: universal exposure across much of the country with partial recourse.
